neighbours.label: the predicate saying whom circumstances favour or punish (not kind to, unforgiving, belongs to [a people/era], was with them), versus the same words in literal location or ownership senses
fire: The winters up north have never been kind to old wooden houses.
Critics were not kind to the director's second film.
The desert is an unforgiving place for anyone who runs out of water.
Many in the crowd shouted that the city belongs to its workers.
History has been kind to the president who once seemed a failure.
Luck was with the climbers, and the weather held for the summit.
Time has not been kind to the old seaside hotel.
The market is unforgiving to companies that ignore their customers.
quiet: The winters up north are often spent inside old wooden houses.
Critics wrote long reviews of the director's second film.
The desert is a hot place for anyone who travels in summer.
Many in the crowd shouted that the city needs more workers.
History books describe the president who once seemed a failure.
The climbers carried ropes, and the weather held for the summit.
The old seaside hotel was painted blue last spring.
The market is open to companies that sell local produce.
